mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) signals robust labor market conditions that support corporate earnings growth and consumer spending, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days without regime dependence.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of months when PAYEMS increases (measured over 12-month rolling windows).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 4.0%, it indicates a tightening labor market that accelerates consumer spending and corporate profit growth, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 20 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:UNRATE as of 2023-05-15 is 4.1% (just above threshold)
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when UNRATE < 4.0% over the last 5 years.

mechanism_narrative: The joint behavior of rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and elevated inflation (CPIAUCSL > 245) signals an aggressive monetary tightening cycle that increases equity discount rates and reduces risk appetite, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL > 245 over the last 5 years.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion regimes, a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals manufacturing sector weakness that precedes corporate earnings deterioration, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansion periods, SPX 20-day returns are positive when INDPRO declines in more than 50% of cases over the last 5 years.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) fall below 1100 thousand units, it indicates weakening residential construction and consumer confidence, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when HOUST < 1100 over the last 5 years.

mechanism_narrative: A rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) consistently increases the cost of capital and reduces equity valuation multiples, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days regardless of economic conditions.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS rises (measured over 12-month rolling windows).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 (index base 2017=100) signals manufacturing contraction that precedes economic slowdown, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when INDPRO < 100 over the last 5 years.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer demand that drives corporate revenue growth, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of months when RSAFS increases (measured over 12-month rolling windows).
